subject: Request: temporary GPU family regrade + 72h burst window for training run
messages:
From: Ellis Brown <ellis.brown@soteria.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@soteria.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary GPU family regrade + 72h burst window for training run

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary of what we need to get over the line from our side: we have a large model re-training job scheduled for Q1 that spikes memory and compute for ~72 continuous hours. Our infra team prefers an A100L32-style SKU for cost predictability, but the training benefits from an H100-class burst for a short window (to finish a critical epoch).

Ask: can Redwood provision a temporary GPU-family regrade — keep our reserved A100L baseline for normal inference, and allow a 72-hour H100 burst window attached to our Dedicated reservation with an overage cap (not-to-exceed) set at $4,500/day for that window? We also need a short reservation hold on the new capacity while we perform a controlled switchover (to avoid preemption during the burst).

I've attached the workload profile and our SOW with the timeline. We understand non-standard terms and are prepared to accept a one-time surcharge for the burst, but we can't accept open-ended overages.

Can you advise next steps and what approvals you need from us (PO, signatures)?

Thanks,
Ellis Brown
Head of ML Ops | Soteria Health
ellis.brown@soteria.ai

Attachments: Soteria_ML_Workload_Profile.csv, Soteria_SOW_redlines_v1.pdf

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Ellis Brown <ellis.brown@soteria.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary GPU family regrade + 72h burst window for training run

Ellis —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachments. We're looped in and prepping a brief for Deal Desk. Quick clarifications before we escalate:
- Confirm the exact 72-hour window target (start/end UTC) so engineering can reserve capacity.
- Is the $4,500/day overage cap a hard ceiling or a target?
- Confirm whether the burst must be H100M or if H100S/H100-variant is acceptable (we have several compatible H100 options).

I'll route to Karthik and Marissa for pricing + terms, then escalate to executive signoff if needed for the reservation hold and nonstandard overage cap. We may need a short addendum to your SOW.

Irene Choi

Irene / Marissa —

Forwarding Soteria's ask. Quick internal pricing notes: baseline A100L pricing as reserved is unchanged. For a 72-hour burst on an H100-class SKU we recommend structuring as a capped overage with a flat daily burst premium; given the customer's size and multi-year intent we can propose a 15% discount on the burst premium if we cap at $4,500/day.

Risks / panels: 1) reservation hold is non-standard for burst windows — engineering will need an explicit hold (no preemption) for those 72 hours; that triggers capacity gating with our resource team and may require a short uplift on committed units. 2) we should require PO + signoff on a one-page addendum enumerating the cap and fallback (if H100 not available, degrade to H100-compatible variant with prorated credit).

My recommended ask for Execs: temporary non-cancelable hold for the 72h window, overage cap $4,500/day (15% discount applied to burst premium), one-time administrative surcharge of $2,500 for hold & priority routing.

If Marissa is good, I'll draft the addendum and route to execs for sign-off.

- Karthik

Vivek —

We're requesting an exec exception and sign-off on a one-off reservation hold and capped overage for Soteria Health (Deal RDW-2027-311). Summary for decision:
- Customer: Soteria Health (prospect moving to Dedicated)
- Request: 72-hour H100-class burst attached to A100L reserved baseline; reservation hold (no preemption) for the burst window; overage capped at $4,500/day.
- Commercial: proposed one-time admin surcharge $2,500 + 15% discount on burst premium (to land at $4,500/day cap).
- Operational impact: engineering will gate capacity for the requested window; may require temporary uplift on other short reservations or use of a spare H100 pool.
- Reasons to approve: high likelihood of expansion, multi-year procurement underway, and Soteria brings strong privacy/compliance requirements (good fit for Dedicated/Private later).

Recommended approval language: "Approved: one-time reservation hold for the specified 72-hour window; overage capped at $4,500/day; charge one-time $2,500 administrative fee; if H100 family unavailable, automatically fallback to highest-capable compatible H100-variant with prorated credit."

Requesting your sign-off or any edits. If you approve, we will: 1) issue an addendum and DocuSign; 2) instruct infra to place a 72h hold; 3) bill the admin fee on next invoice.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
